image_description: A grey whale surfacing in calm, grey ocean waters. The whale's head and upper back are visible above the waterline, with a distinct spout of mist rising from its blowholes. The skin appears dark grey and mottled. The background consists of a hazy horizon line where the sea meets the sky.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head shape is consistent with a grey whale, showing a blunt, arched rostrum. A spout is clearly visible, indicating the presence and function of blowholes, although the holes themselves are partially obscured by the spray and angle.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin exhibits the characteristic mottled grey coloration with lighter, irregular patches consistent with barnacle encrustations found on grey whales.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image only captures the anterior portion (head and shoulders) of the whale. The posterior back where dorsal knuckles would be located is submerged or outside the frame, making this feature impossible to verify.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the head and immediate shoulder area are visible. The full spindle-shaped body is not in view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with the head checkpoint, the visible upper body skin shows the correct mottled texture and coloration.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The whale's mouth is closed and underwater; baleen plates are internal structures not visible in this external surfacing shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The pectoral fins are located on the underside/lateral aspects of the body and are completely submerged/occluded in this view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is entirely out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin surface appears textured and uneven, consistent with the rough texture and callosities described for grey whales.

alignment_reasoning: The image strongly aligns with the 'grey whale' class. All testable checkpoints regarding head shape, skin mottling/coloration, and texture are present and accurate. Several checkpoints were marked untestable due to the framing (only the head is visible), but there are no contradictions in the visible data. The spout and barnacle patterns are highly specific to this species.
